info.name: Hetzner Cloud Actions Load Balancers API

params.name: sort
params.description:
Sort resources by field and direction. May be used multiple times.

For more information, see "[Sorting](#description/sorting)".

params.name: name
params.description:
Filter resources by their name.

The response will only contain the resources
matching exactly the specified name.

params.name: label_selector
params.description:
Filter resources by labels.

The response will only contain resources matching the label selector.
For more information, see "[Label Selector](#description/label-selector)".

params.name: page
params.description: Page number to return. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".

params.name: per_page
params.description: Maximum number of entries returned per page. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".

items.docs: Gets all existing Load Balancers that you have available.

Creates a Load Balancer.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `412` | `source_port_already_used` | The source port you are trying to add is already in use |
| `422` | `ip_not_owned` | The IP is not owned by the owner of the project of the Load Balancer |
| `422` | `load_balancer_not_attached_to_network` | The Load Balancer is not attached to a network |
| `422` | `resolve_cloud_private_targets_error` | The server you are trying to add as a target
Gets a specific Load Balancer object.

Updates a Load Balancer. You can update a Load Balancer’s name and a Load Balancer’s labels.

Note: if the Load Balancer object changes during the request, the response will be a “conflict” error.

params.name: start
params.description: Start of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).

params.name: end
params.description: End of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).

items.docs:
You must specify the type of metric to get: `open_connections`, `connections_per_second`, `requests_per_second` or `bandwidth`. You can also specify more than one type by comma separation, e.g. `requests_per_second,bandwidth`.

Depending on the type you will get different time series data:

|Type | Timeseries | Unit | Description |
|---- |------------|------|-------------|
| open_connections | open_connections | number | Open connections |
| connections_per_second | connections_per_second | conn
